clue.text: Two little boys like Basil?

parts.note: Herb is a short form of the boy's name Herbert
Al is a short form of the boy's name Albert or Alan

explanation.surface: Two small lads are compared with someone called Basil.
explanation.walkthrough: The one phrase 'Two little boys' gives two short names, HERB and AL. Basil looks like a man's name, but here it is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a culinary herb, so something like it is plant-based in the herbal sense; the question mark flags a definition by example.

clue.text: As part of text, remit your final piece

indicators.note: As part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction to send back the last part of the essay.
explanation.definitionFit: The extreme end or outermost part of something is its final piece.

clue.text: British girl in faraway land

parts.note: Olivia is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A British woman living in a distant country.
explanation.definitionFit: This landlocked South American country is a distant land from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Flower arrangement — this surely is laid-back

definitions.text: Flower arrangement — this surely is laid-back

parts.words: Flower arrangement — this surely is laid-back
parts.note: a garland of blossoms from Hawaii, a place famed for its relaxed, laid-back way of life

explanation.definitionFit: A Hawaiian garland is a ring of flowers worn round the neck, an arrangement of blooms.

clue.text: Shoot a trouble-maker in European city

parts.note: a bud is a young shoot on a plant
a pest is a nuisance, someone who makes trouble

explanation.surface: Someone opens fire on an agitator somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' reads as a verb about firing a gun, but it is the noun for a new growth on a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hungary's capital is a major city on the Danube in central Europe.

clue.text: A court's conclusion after petition is produced

indicators.note: after means the following letters come behind the word for petition

parts.note: to beg is to petition or plead

indicators.note: conclusion means only the last letter of court's is taken

explanation.surface: A judge's final ruling comes after a plea is put forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word; 'produced' is the old biblical sense of fathering.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic past tense of beget means fathered, so produced offspring, as in biblical genealogies.

clue.text: Repeatedly test very strong chess move

definitions.meaning: to verify again, testing a second time
a move putting the king under attack from two pieces at once

explanation.definitionFit: To verify twice is to test again, and in chess two pieces attacking the king together is a powerful move.

clue.text: Artist having abnormal cravings to eat thus

parts.note: pica is the medical term for an abnormal craving to eat non-food substances; plural here
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A painter with strange appetites who eats in this manner.
explanation.walkthrough: PICA is a medical term: a craving to eat things like chalk or soil.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism is one of the most famous artists of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Scottish island ultimately lacking a workforce

indicators.note: ultimately lacking means the letter is removed from the end of the island's name

parts.note: Staffa is a small island in the Inner Hebrides, home of Fingal's Cave

explanation.surface: A remote Scottish island ends up short of workers.
explanation.walkthrough: STAFFA is a small Hebridean island off western Scotland; drop its final A.
explanation.definitionFit: The employees of an organisation are collectively its workforce, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Carefully following second conversation

parts.note: talking is conversation, chat between people

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly trails a person during a second chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Shadowing a person or animal closely and stealthily is the hunter's or pursuer's sense of the word.

clue.text: Relative cut down a drug, initially, having abandoned habit

indicators.note: cut down means the word for the relative is shortened, losing its final letter

parts.note: an uncle is a family relative

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the word drug is used

explanation.surface: A family member reduced his drug use and gave up a bad habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' sounds like an addiction, but it is clothing, like a monk's habit; to abandon it is to strip.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a garment, so someone who has shed their clothes is naked or undressed.

clue.text: Lead, say, loud form of musical performance

definitions.meaning: lead is an example of a dense, weighty metallic element
a style of loud, aggressive amplified rock music

explanation.definitionFit: Lead is literally a heavy metal, and the phrase also names a loud genre of rock music.

clue.text: Girl admits Duke wrongly called less than noble

indicators.note: admits means the word for girl takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young unmarried woman

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters of called are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A young woman concedes that a duke was mistakenly described as not aristocratic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' looks like confessing, but it means letting in; 'less than noble' is fair because this class sits below the aristocracy.
explanation.definitionFit: The bourgeois social rank sits below the aristocracy, so it is less than noble.

clue.text: Piano frequently accompanying start of song

indicators.note: start of means only the opening letter of the word song is taken

parts.note: oft is an old word meaning often or frequently

explanation.surface: A piano is often played along with the opening of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piano' looks like the instrument, but in music it is the direction meaning play quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: In musical notation piano is the Italian term for quiet, a direction to play gently.

clue.text: Site of a historical listed building

definitions.text: Site of a historical listed building

parts.words: Site of a historical listed building
parts.note: a listed building in Britain is a protected one, but listed here also means leaning, so this is the city of a famous leaning tower

explanation.definitionFit: This Tuscan city is home to the famous medieval bell tower that leans to one side.

clue.text: Wake-up calls

parts.note: not alarm calls from a hotel but the songs that birds sing at first light, which wake people

explanation.definitionFit: The singing of many birds at daybreak acts as nature's alarm call to rouse sleepers.

clue.text: Not prepared to turn up for a series of engagements

indicators.note: in a down answer to turn up means the word is read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: raw means unprepared or uncooked

explanation.surface: Someone unready to appear for a round of appointments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagements' suggests appointments or betrothals, but here they are battles.
explanation.definitionFit: A conflict consists of a series of military engagements, that is battles.

clue.text: General, in vain, rules otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means the letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: An army general who rules in vain might do things differently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army officer, but it is the adjective; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying to all cases, the answer and general are adjectival synonyms.

clue.text: Amend range, badly for the most part

indicators.note: to amend is to alter, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone told to correct a poorly made range of goods, for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amend' at the front is the anagram signal; 'badly' looks like a second one but is fodder, its letters joining those of 'range'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means generally or on the whole, the same as mostly.

clue.text: Political recovery plan that follows a reshuffle?

definitions.meaning: Roosevelt's 1930s programme to lift the USA out of the Depression
after a pack of cards is shuffled, the next round of cards dealt out is a fresh one

explanation.definitionFit: Roosevelt's economic programme of the 1930s bore this name, and a fresh deal of cards follows reshuffling.

clue.text: Impudent youngster, note

definitions.meaning: a cheeky, forward young person, especially a girl
a short written note, such as a voucher or memo

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a saucy young girl and a brief note or IOU slip.

clue.text: Man destroyed after elevation of Roman Catholic queen

definitions.text: Man destroyed after elevation of Roman Catholic queen

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters come behind the raised abbreviation
in a down answer elevation means the abbreviation is raised up, reading upwards
destroyed means the letters of man are wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for a queen

explanation.surface: A man was put to death after a Catholic queen came to the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the Protestant Archbishop of Canterbury was burned at the stake after Mary I, a Roman Catholic queen, was elevated to the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: The Archbishop of Canterbury under Henry VIII was burned in 1556 under the Catholic Mary I.

clue.text: Expression that's sullen, almost? Lighter

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a scowl is a sullen, angry look on the face

explanation.surface: Asking whether a sullen look is almost brighter than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' looks like a comparison, but it is the noun for a flat-bottomed barge.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a flat boat used to unload ships, and this flat-bottomed barge is one kind.

clue.text: Top flier reputedly going straight North

parts.note: the saying 'as the crow flies' means in a straight line, so this bird is the flier

explanation.surface: A leading bird is said to be heading due north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reputedly' is not a homophone signal here; it refers to the saying 'as the crow flies'.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown of the head or of a hill is its top, the highest part.

clue.text: Creator of instrument heard in Haydn symphony

definitions.text: Creator of instrument heard in Haydn symphony

parts.words: Creator of instrument heard in Haydn symphony
parts.note: Haydn's Symphony No 101 is nicknamed after the ticking device suggested by its slow movement; the person who builds that device

explanation.definitionFit: Haydn's 101st symphony is nicknamed for the timepiece its ticking slow movement evokes, and the craftsman who builds such timepieces fits.

clue.text: Power of speech, nothing indelicate

parts.note: O, the figure zero, stands for nothing
racy means risqué or indelicate

explanation.surface: Eloquence that contains nothing improper.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is coined on literacy to mean skill in spoken expression, the power of speech.

clue.text: Short time to study a city in Italy

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a brief time
a den is a private room for study or work

explanation.surface: Someone has only a brief spell to learn about an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: This northern Italian city in Emilia-Romagna is known for balsamic vinegar and sports cars.

clue.text: Film put on of wing flapping excessively

indicators.note: put on means the film word is added to follow the word for wing

parts.note: alar is an adjective meaning relating to wings
a mist is a thin film, as on glass

explanation.surface: A movie is screened about wings beating wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' suggests cinema but is a thin coating; 'flapping' in British slang means panicking.
explanation.definitionFit: To flap is British slang for panicking, so someone given to excessive panic is a scaremonger.

clue.text: Music broadcast

definitions.meaning: to put out on radio or television

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a melody and to transmit a programme, as in going on air.

clue.text: Island rejected agreement on fish

indicators.note: on means the reversed word is placed after the word for fish

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

indicators.note: rejected means the word for agreement is turned back, reading backwards

parts.note: yes is a word of agreement

explanation.surface: An island turned down a deal over fishing rights.
explanation.definitionFit: This large island lies off the north-west coast of Wales across the Menai Strait.

clue.text: Artist goes to bank seldom

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: A painter visits the bank only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a building for money; here it is the verb, as in 'bank on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seldom and the answer are adverbial synonyms, both meaning not often.
